title: Boombox
description: The Sharp - small but toothy radio and cassette recorder, connected to the computer.
details: The Sharp GF-7 boombox is connected to the computer using regular audio cables. You used to use it to store programs on cassette tapes, but now you have a floppy disk drive for that. And yet you store your software archives on tapes. Some Commodore programs can also output sound to it. And with the ability to record songs from the radio or capture live audio using the external microphones, the possibilities are endless. Everything works fine, but the magnetic head needs to be adjusted frequently with a screwdriver, and the cassette deck needs to be secured with duct tape.
